intent: The lion kingdom nobody names: three safari countries, one holds most of the world's lions — then the shock number of how few are left anywhere, and the one place outside Africa that still has them.
pacing_profile: question read verbatim, three options, 3-s beat, reveal with the number, story beats shaped per episode (brief.md), punchline + short follow
pause_policy: Pause only at the marked ellipses; the beat is real silence (ticks come from quizscore.py).
title: Where do MOST of the world's wild lions live?

lines.direction: the question, cold — curiosity comes from the map moving under it
lines.text: Where do most of the world's wild lions live?

lines.direction: quick, each option its own beat

lines.text: Tanzania. Its latest count found some 17,000 lions, more than all the other countries on Earth put together.

lines.direction: pull back to show the three safari countries; South Africa and Kenya light dim with their counts on 'Africa' and 'Kenya'; the continent counter runs to 23,000 and stops on 'lions'
lines.text: South Africa has some 3,000 and Kenya even fewer. All of Africa holds just 23,000 wild lions.

lines.direction: wide on the whole continent; the percent counter climbs to 94 and the sad flag-ball pops on 'roamed'
lines.text: Lions have now gone from 94 percent of all the land they once roamed.

lines.direction: fly north-east across the Arabian Sea; India lights on 'India', the Gir tag lands, the ASIATIC LIONS card on 'Asiatic', lion sticker throbs
lines.text: Outside Africa, only Gir, in India, still has any at all: nearly 900 Asiatic lions, and nowhere else.

lines.direction: punchline, then a short follow — the outro visual asks
lines.text: Far fewer than you thought. Follow us.
